# pengdows.efcore.conformance

> Black-box conformance tests for relational providers of Entity Framework Core 10.

## Purpose

This repository tests externally observable behavior through documented EF Core public APIs. The provider is configured through an adapter, operations run through `DbContext`, LINQ, and EF Core relational APIs, and results are asserted through fresh contexts or documented public state.

## Boundary

- Do not inspect generated SQL, EF provider services, EF internals, or provider implementation types in shared tests.
- Keep provider setup and database provisioning in `IProviderAdapter` implementations.
- Capabilities declare applicability only. They never alter expected values or assertions.
- Strict runs require a supported or unsupported declaration for every feature in `ProviderCapabilities.KnownFeatures`.
- ADO.NET `DataTypes` metadata is the preferred native type inventory. Mark catalog evidence independent only when it is independent of the EF model. Types read from test-created tables are `SELF_DERIVED` and excluded from coverage totals.
- Run the same test assembly against one provider per process. Compare report JSON with the runner's `--compare` command.

## Project map

- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Contracts/`: adapter contracts, capabilities, type discovery, and outcomes.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner/`: adapter loading, test execution, JSON/JUnit reports, type discovery, and cross-provider comparison.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Inventory/`: reflection-generated EF Core public API inventory.
- `tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/`: shared EF Core 10 relational behavioral tests.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/`: Microsoft provider reference adapter; included in the standalone solution.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.PengdowsSqlite/`: pengdows adapter; depends on the separate pengdows ADO.NET repository and is intentionally outside the solution build.
- `manifests/`: EF Core 10 contract and generated API inventory.

## Build and run

```sh
dotnet build pengdows.efcore.conformance.slnx
export PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING='Data Source=/tmp/efcore-reference.db'
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --run \
  tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational.csproj \
  "$PWD/adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/bin/Debug/net10.0/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.dll" \
  pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.MicrosoftSqliteAdapter /tmp/efcore-reference-report
```

Run the same test assembly for another provider with a separate disposable database and report directory. Compare results:

```sh
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --compare \
  /tmp/candidate-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/efcore-reference-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/provider-comparison.json
```

Append `--cleanup-database` to `--run` only when the configured database is dedicated and disposable. The runner then calls the adapter cleanup hook after writing test results.

## Provider configuration

The sibling ADO.NET conformance project uses `providers/*.json` profiles to describe driver, target, connection string, environment, dialect, and type inventory. The EF Core harness borrows declarative per-provider profiles for adapter selection and connection strings: `profiles/*.json` names a compiled adapter assembly/type and a connection string template with `${ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE}` placeholders. Run one with `--run-profile <profile.json> <test-project> <report-directory> [--cleanup-database]`. Adapter assembly paths are relative to the profile file unless absolute.

EF profiles deliberately leave EF provider configuration, capabilities, database initialization, and cleanup in `IProviderAdapter`. A profile cannot change expectations or assertions. Profiles do not provision containers or remote databases; infrastructure setup remains external. The old direct `--run` form and `PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING` are still supported.

## Current status

- EF Core baseline: 10.0.14 on `net10.0`.
- The public API inventory is generated from the Core, Abstractions, Relational, and Design assemblies. Disposition rules in `manifests/efcore-10.json` attach rationales to EF-owned and provider-service surfaces; tests override those rules. Current counts: 18,795 entries, 737 overload entries linked to runtime behavioral families, 0 uncovered member families, 0 entries awaiting classification, 3,532 EF-owned entries, and 8,357 provider-service or model-configuration entries marked not directly applicable. Applicable Design behavior is tested; remaining tooling and dependency wiring has explicit provider-applicability rationales.
- Latest full runs execute 344 cases on SQLite (pengdows 319 pass / 10 fail / 15 unsupported; Microsoft 324 / 5 / 15), 404 on Pomelo MySQL (387 / 5 / 12), and 382 on Npgsql PostgreSQL (374 / 7 / 1). Each run includes two passing public EF Design scenarios for migration code generation/scaffolding and reverse-engineering model helpers. MySQL also includes 62 generated native type mapping cases and PostgreSQL 40; all pass. Each type case inserts through EF Core and reads through a fresh context. Six nullable/default/cancellation cases pass on every provider. Five failures (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched-row `RightJoin`, and sync/async TPT save counts) reproduce on all providers. Five decimal fidelity failures are pengdows-only. PostgreSQL also fails `Least`/`Greatest` translation on sync and async paths. Reference-provider failures support triage but do not prove an EF Core defect.
- Added optional Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 and Npgsql/PostgreSQL 17 adapters and profiles. MySQL passes 386/403 cases, including 62 generated native type round trips, with five shared failures and 12 explicit unsupported results. PostgreSQL passes 373/381 cases, including 40 generated native type round trips, with seven failures and one unsupported result. SQLite declares ambient `System.Transactions` and independent native-type discovery unsupported, while MySQL passes sync and async enlistment. Both SQLite adapters pass sync/async `ReferentialAction.SetDefault` migration tests. Database-collation migration passes on Pomelo MySQL and is unsupported on SQLite and PostgreSQL.
- Independent ADO.NET type discovery now drives per-type tests from the adapter's declarative CLR/store-type mapping profile. MySQL Connector reports 51 metadata rows / 41 native names; 30 type/mapping rows pass generated sync/async fidelity and 16 are unlinked. Npgsql reports 133 rows/names including arrays and ranges; 19 type rows pass and 114 are unlinked. Run outputs place the actual outcomes in `ado-net-types.json`. `UNLINKED` means the adapter does not claim a mapping; it is not a provider failure. SQLite does not advertise `DataTypes`, so its supplemental test-schema evidence is self-derived and excluded from independent coverage.
- SQLite ADO.NET providers do not advertise `DataTypes`. Supplemental types discovered from test-created schema are self-derived; independent native type coverage is not currently established for SQLite.
- Public type declarations, compiler-generated enum backing fields, and inherited `System.Object` overrides carry explicit non-applicability rationales because they are inventory nodes or EF-owned object behavior rather than provider operations. The test suite is a growing conformance slice, not yet complete coverage of every applicable EF Core public API. Consult `README.md`, `manifests/efcore-10.json`, and `manifests/efcore-10-api-inventory.json` for disposition rules, current counts, rationales, and uncovered members.


## Unfinished work

Inventory dimensions overlap: uncovered member families are distinct from APIs given explicit non-applicability rationales.

1. Classification: the Core, Abstractions, Relational, and Design inventories now have zero unclassified entries and zero uncovered member families. Reverse-engineering helpers and migration generator/scaffolder output have behavioral links; provider dependency bags, project file removal, and bundle entry points have explicit black-box applicability rationales. Review those rationales as EF contracts evolve. PostgreSQL exercises sequence, schema, and schema-qualified function APIs; database-collation migration is unsupported on PostgreSQL and SQLite. `MigrationBuilder` operation-list construction and inspection are excluded as EF-owned in-memory behavior.
2. Expand behavioral matrices across all families. Add overload, boundary, failure, composition, and interaction cases; run sync and async paths independently. Linkage alone does not mean an overload or scenario executed.
3. Triage the five pengdows-only decimal fidelity failures, the five failures reproduced across all four providers (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched `RightJoin`, sync/async TPT save counts), and two PostgreSQL-only failures (sync/async `Least`/`Greatest`) against documented contracts. Reproduction on a reference provider is evidence, not proof of an EF Core defect.
4. Expand native-type fidelity. MySQL and PostgreSQL now generate sync/async insert and fresh-context retrieval tests for declared mappings; all current generated cases pass. Add update, null, boundary, parameterization, and applicable query scenarios, expand adapter profiles to cover more discovered types, and compare ADO.NET metadata with database catalogs.
5. Expand beyond the first Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 run to additional relational providers and server versions, keeping shared expectations provider-independent and capability declarations explicit.
6. Add a separate EF Core 11 target after its release contract is established; generate its inventory from its actual assemblies and add version-specific tests for changed or new behavior.

EF Core 10 completion requires zero unclassified entries, behavioral or justified disposition for each applicable public API family, sync/async coverage where both APIs exist, independently discovered native-type coverage, triaged failures, and reports that distinguish pass, fail, unsupported, infrastructure error, and uncovered work. The latest runs cover 344 SQLite, 404 MySQL, and 382 PostgreSQL cases. Every inventoried Design member now has a test link or an explicit applicability rationale; review those rationales as EF contracts evolve. Native type operations beyond insert/readback also remain.
